## Drafter's flagged points — decided

- **15.424 (stop vs repeat).** Kept the shipped repeat, with its full stop (“…pointed out her father’s high-roofed
  house.”). Conventions: a repeated line gets the same English every time; validator check 6 fails a whole-unit
  repeat whose `l`/`i` differ at all; the packet says “must be identical”. A colon before the woman's speech would read better, but
  the rule outranks it. Greek still ends ·; the English stop is the shipped one.
- **“answered with a word” vs shipped “answered in speech” (434, 439).** Kept “with a word” in `l`. Conventions rows 9.506
  and 10.71 fix ἠμείβετο μύθῳ as “answered … with a word” and say so in their avoided columns; the only
  shipped “in speech” is odyssey-027 line 67 (a different formula, not a unit repeat, so the validator does not
  bind it). Left as shipped there; recorded here as an inconsistency for the LOG, not corrected in a published part.
- **new-renderings.md rows.** All 19 rows checked against the units: each matches `l`/`i` and the note
  carries the “sense not certain” flags the rows ask for (πολυπαίπαλοι, ὁδαῖα, ῥυδόν, ὠμῷ, ἐπίβαθρον, Συρίη).
  τρῶκται (row 14.289 “a gnawer / a rogue”), εὐεργός (11.434), ἰδυῖα, ἀπήμων, κερδαλέος, δαΐφρων, θυμός
  (“life” 2, “heart” 14, “heart and spirit” 25), τανύπεπλος, ἴφθιμος, ἀθέσφατος, ἀλλόθροοι, ὄρχαμος ἀνδρῶν follow existing house rows.
  Words lacking a row that will probably recur (to add when rows are copied, optional): περιπληθής (“very populous”),
  τροπαὶ ἠελίοιο (“turnings of the sun”, sense flagged in the note), ἀτιτάλλω (“bring up / nurse”).

## Quotation marks (speeches)

- Open at 352 → now closed at 376 (error above). Odysseus 381–388: “ … ” correct (stops at 388, before the narrator's 389).
- Eumaeus's second speech opens “ at 390 in both layers and is deliberately **left open** at 453: nothing in the Greek
  ends it (no closing formula; the story of the Phoenician woman is still being told), so it runs into the next part, as
  odyssey-011 → 012 did. The validator will WARN “3 opening and 2 closing” for each layer: expected; **LOG.md must say that
  Eumaeus's speech from 390 runs on into odyssey-076**, whose first unit must carry no opening “ and no `mark`.
- Inner speeches, single ‘ ’ inside Eumaeus's: woman 425–429 (‘ at 425, ’ at 429); man 431–433 (‘ ’); woman 435–436 (‘ ’);
  woman 440–453 (‘ at 440, ’ at 453). All opened and closed, each opener carries a `mark`. The narrator's formulas at
  430, 434, 437–439 sit between them, unquoted, inside the open outer speech, which is correct.
- `p` flags checked against the packet's ¶ (351, 380, 389, 403, 415, 425, 430, 434, 437, 440): all present, no extras.

## Findings considered and refused

1. 351/389 reply-formula vs 380 etc.: l/i identical to published or table rows; nothing to change.
2. 374 note “ὑπερφίαλος … is translated the same wherever it is used of men”: reads as a statement of house practice
   (rows 6.274, 9.106), not a claim about the poem; kept.
3. 374 note naming Penelope and the suitors: hedged by “the text names neither”; kept.
4. 361 i omits τί (“somewhat”) and 365 i adds “only”: smoothing in the plain layer, l carries both; kept.
5. 386 i “with the sheep or the cattle” for παρ’ οἴεσιν ἢ παρὰ βουσίν (l has “beside”): idiomatic; kept.
6. 403 l “very populous, so very much”: renders περι- as “very” (house practice) plus λίην τόσον; kept.
7. 445 ὦνον as “purchase” (l) beside “price” at 388, 429, 452: same noun, note says both senses; kept.
8. Syrie (not Syria): new-renderings row justifies it and the note says it is not the later country; kept.
9. 437 note “ἔφαθ’ is ἔφατο elided”: standard; kept.
10. 442 ἐπιφράσσετ’ as short-vowel subjunctive: defensible after μή; kept.
11. ASCII apostrophes in `l`/`i` (“man's”): every shipped part uses them; kept.
12. Remembered English in `i`: none detected; every distinctive phrase (“chief of men”, “of many wiles”, “trinkets”, “rogues”,
    “a raw old age”, “immense”) is a house row, and the rest was rebuilt from the case relations. Greek → `l` word by word
    done for all 59 units; l ↔ i agree in sense and force except the points above.
